response_json.request: Design a fixation rod mounted from the top with arm length 200mm to have ability to fix cutting product

actions.operation: Create a fixation rod having an arm.
actions.relational_constraint: The stated 200 mm length applies to the arm of the fixation rod.
actions.unresolved_reference: The arm geometry, its length-defining endpoints, and its direction are not specified.
steps: Create the fixation rod as a new, separate CAD component rather than merging it permanently with the existing single-piece bracket. Use section S05, the upper interface head and threaded boss, as the parent localization reference.

Extract the center axis of the threaded axial bore from face 0031 (FACE 29). Use this y-direction axis as the principal mounting axis of the new rod and as the datum from which the arm position is controlled.

Use boss top annulus face 0032 (FACE 6) as the mounting-height datum. Reference boss entry chamfer face 0033 (FACE 4) for insertion clearance and boss outer-cylinder face 0034 (FACE 5) for radial-envelope checking.

Create a datum plane passing through the bore axis and the intended arm direction. The preferred functional direction is horizontally toward the accessible C-frame throat or the cutting-product location, but retain the direction as a configurable assembly parameter until the machine layout is confirmed.

Sketch the axial mounting stem on a plane containing the bore axis. Include a threaded engagement portion, a shoulder or collar above the boss, and a transition into the arm. Size the stem and thread to match the actual internal thread represented by face 0031; thread standard, pitch, fit class, engagement length, and stem diameter remain to be measured or specified.

Revolve the mounting-stem profile about the extracted y-axis, or extrude a circular stem coaxially with face 0031. Model a shoulder underside capable of seating against face 0032 without contacting the bore-entry edge or chamfer.

Model the arm from the upper end of the stem. For a round fixation rod, sketch a centerline path with a vertical-to-horizontal transition and sweep a circular section along it. For a manufactured clamp bar, alternatively sketch a rectangular arm profile on the datum plane and extrude it symmetrically about the model mid-depth plane z=-21 mm.

Apply the 200 mm driving dimension to the arm. Because the request does not define the endpoints, initially define arm length as the horizontal distance from the mounting-bore axis to the distal clamping axis; expose this definition as a named parameter so it can be changed if the intended dimension is instead overall arm length or straight-segment length.

Add a generous bend radius or fillet at the junction between the vertical mounting stem and the horizontal arm to reduce bending stress. Determine rod diameter, arm section, and fillet radius from the required clamping force, 200 mm bending moment, material, and allowable deflection.

Create a distal fixation interface at the end of the arm. Prefer a downward-facing threaded hole or guided clamp-spindle feature aligned with the product-support region, followed by a replaceable swivel pressure pad to avoid marking the cutting product. Keep spindle thread, travel, pad diameter, and vertical reach parameterized because the workpiece dimensions are not provided.

Add practical edge breaks or chamfers to exposed arm ends and the stem entry. Avoid sharp transitions in the main load path, and verify that the new component does not collide with the boss blends, top shoulders, C-frame webs, or the product-loading opening.

Assign the new fixation rod a suitable high-strength material and perform a static check using the maximum intended clamping force at the 200 mm lever arm. Validate stem thread shear, arm bending stress, junction stress concentration, boss loading, and operational deflection before releasing the design.

actions.operation: Mount the fixation rod from the top.
actions.target: The fixation rod created in the preceding action and the top of the existing model
actions.relational_constraint: The fixation rod must be mounted from the top.
actions.unresolved_reference: The specific top face or top mounting feature, mounting position, and mounting orientation must be identified from the CAD model.
steps: Localize the top mounting interface in section S05. The primary receiving feature is threaded axial bore face 0031 (FACE 29), visible concentrically in the top and isometric views; the primary seating datum is boss top annulus face 0032 (FACE 6).

Insert the fixation-rod component from above the model, along the positive-to-negative y direction, with its threaded stem coaxial to face 0031. Apply a concentric assembly constraint between the stem and the cylindrical bore axis.

Apply a thread or screw mate matching the existing bore thread. Do not remove or enlarge section S05 unless thread inspection establishes that the existing interface is incompatible with the required fixation-rod load.

Seat the rod collar, shoulder, or a hardened washer against boss top annulus face 0032. Apply a coincident or contact constraint between these seating surfaces while maintaining clearance from boss entry chamfer face 0033 and boss outer-cylinder face 0034.

Orient the 200 mm arm horizontally toward the cutting-product clamping zone and away from the bracket body. Confirm clearance throughout installation and adjustment against the rectangular upper head, the curved C-frame spine, and the side-access throat.

Provide rotational locking after the arm reaches its working orientation. Preferred methods are a jam nut on the threaded stem, a split collar, or a keyed shoulder so that clamping reaction does not unscrew the mounting stem.

Inspect the existing transverse-hole segments identified by faces 0039 (FACE 2) and 0040 (FACE 3). If the transverse hole intersects the axial bore as indicated by section S05, it may be used as an optional cross-pin or secondary retention feature after a matching hole or retention groove is added to the new stem. Verify alignment and remaining stem cross-section before adopting this method.

Preserve the existing top boss, annular blends, and shoulders because they distribute the rod's axial and bending loads into the primary C-frame. No removal of sections S01 through S04 is required for the requested top-mounted rod.

Check that the assembled arm and clamp spindle can reach the cutting product while leaving adequate loading, tool, and cutting clearance. Confirm that the clamp force is directed into a suitable support or fixture surface rather than into an unsupported part of the product.

Run interference checks in the installation, adjustment, and clamping positions. Then verify thread engagement, seating contact, anti-rotation retention, arm deflection, bracket overturning load, and the mounting-flange fastener reactions before finalizing the assembly.
